summary: Flame in Freefall turns decades of NASA microgravity combustion experiments into practical fire-safety answers for crew habitats on the ISS, the Moon and Mars. NASA's fire research (BASS, Saffire, FLEX, ACME, SAME) is scattered across the Physical Science Informatics (PSI) repository and hard to compare, yet planned lunar habitats will run at roughly 30% oxygen and 10.2 psi, where materials burn far more readily. The dashboard ranks every investigation for a chosen habitat and safety priority, maps which oxygen and pressure conditions have actually been tested, compares experiments side by side, and answers plain-English questions using only NASA records with cited sources. It pairs a hybrid search engine (BM25 + Latent Semantic Analysis, fused with Reciprocal Rank Fusion) with retrieval-augmented generation and a citation guardrail, and ingests real NASA PSI data files directly. Key finding: the planned lunar atmosphere lies outside every solid-material test in the data, even though solids are the main cabin fire load - showing exactly where new experiments are needed.
details:
What it does: Users pick a habitat (ISS, lunar rover, Mars, spacesuit) and a priority -prevention, detection, or suppression. The app ranks all 20 NASA combustion investigations by relevance, maps the oxygen/pressure envelope each experiment tested against crew atmospheres, compares investigations, and answers natural-language questions with cited NASA sources.

How it works: A transparent scoring model (atmosphere fit, fuel relevance, safety-pillar fit, gravity) ranks investigations deterministically - the language model never sets scores. Search combines Okapi BM25 (written from scratch) and Latent Semantic Analysis, fused with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (retrieval MRR 0.98 on a 25-question benchmark). The Ask tab uses retrieval-augmented generation with Google Gemini, constrained to retrieved context, with a citation guardrail that flags unsupported citations and an offline fallback. A robust importer ingests real NASA PSI tables across formats, units, and encodings.

Impact: It converts a scattered archive into an auditable decision tool and pinpoints data gaps for future experiments.

Tools: Python, Streamlit, scikit-learn, Google Gemini, Plotly; deployed on Streamlit Community Cloud with GitHub Actions CI (18 passing tests).
dataRefs: ASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) Data Repository - Combustion Science
